curriculum_alignment.subject: Mathematics
curriculum_alignment.basis: NCERT Class 5 Mathematics concept map for Factors and Multiples
curriculum_alignment.verification_note: Ensure terminology matches local curriculum standards.

prerequisite_diagnostic.purpose: Verify multiplication table fluency and division basics.

items.question: How many groups of 3 can you make from 12 items?

lessons.title: Factors: The Building Blocks
lessons.objective: Learner can find all factors of a given number up to 50.
teach: Define factor as a number that divides another number exactly without a remainder.
Demonstrate finding factors using arrays (e.g., 12 can be 1x12, 2x6, 3x4).
Explain that 1 is a factor of every number.

lessons.title: Multiples: Skip Counting Forward
lessons.objective: Learner can identify and generate multiples of a number.
teach: Define multiple as the product of a number and any whole number.
Explain that a number has an infinite number of multiples.

worked_example.prompt: List the first five multiples of 7.

lessons.title: Common Factors and HCF
lessons.objective: Learner can find common factors and identify the Highest Common Factor (HCF).
teach: List factors of two different numbers.
Identify factors present in both lists.
Select the largest among them as HCF.

worked_example.method: Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Factors of 16: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. Common: 1, 2, 4. HCF is 4.

lessons.mastery_signal: 5 identified as HCF with step-by-step logic.

lessons.title: Common Multiples and LCM
lessons.objective: Learner can find common multiples and identify the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM).
teach: Identify the first multiple that appears in both lists.
Define it as the Lowest Common Multiple.

worked_example.method: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16... Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18... Smallest common is 12.

items.question: Which of these is NOT a factor of 24?
items.explanation: 24 is not divisible by 5 without a remainder.

items.question: Write the first three common multiples of 2 and 3.

misconception_remediation.diagnostic: Ask: Is 10 a factor or multiple of 5?
repair: Use the word 'Few' for Factors and 'Many' for Multiples.
misconception_remediation.exit_criterion: Correctly identifying factors and multiples for 3 different numbers.

mastery_policy.on_failure: Reteach L01 and L02 using visual dot patterns.
